title: Weaker field-size hypothesis and balanced endpoint sizing sharpen the remainder

claims.statement: Joint CircuitBreaker theorem under rules.md: the following declaration defines ONE fixed eligible total uniform NP family in the pinned full B2 model at actual input length n. Its full guarantee and its declared projection both hold unconditionally, for all sufficiently large integer lengths with the quantifiers specified by the theorem kinds. Both score source claims assert this ENTIRE declaration, not separate lemmas. For g(n)=c*n^p*(log2 n)^q*(log2 log2 n)^r with the exact parameters in guarantee, liminf over all integer n of C_B2(f_n)/g(n) >= 1. Equivalently, for every epsilon>0 there is N_epsilon such that C_B2(f_n)>=(1-epsilon)*g(n) for every integer n>=N_epsilon. Declaration: {"convention":"uniform-np-full-b2-actual-length-all-lengths-v1","family":"The single total certificate-prefix language specified in proof.md and family.py. For actual length N, choose k as the least prime at least the least positive B with B^5>((27+18sqrt(2))/64)*N^3, decided exactly by g=64B^5-27N^3>0 and g^2>648N^6; read k input bits as the lower coefficients of a monic degree-k polynomial Q over F_2, reject invalid Q by the exact Frobenius/gcd test, and evaluate the descending-power BK symmetric polynomial on the remaining N-k bits with zero padding, r=ceil((N-k)/k), t=ceil(sqrt(r)). Output 0 for N=0 or the explicit failed guards in proof.md. The output is the constant coefficient in F_2[Z]/Q. All k prefix bits are included in N; Q is input, not advice.","guarantee":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"4"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"polynomial_log","log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"}},"projection":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"4"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"finite"},"theorem":"For the one total uniform polynomial-time certificate-prefix family specified in proof.md and family.py with c=(27+18sqrt(2))/64 and length rule B^5>c*N^3, C_B2(F_N)>=4N-3k-8d_N+7 at every sufficiently large integer N. Put W=r(r+3)/2, H=(t-1)(t+2)/2, A0=(t-1)k-H-(r-t+1), L=floor(t*k/(t+1)-t/2), q=floor(L/t), a=L-t*q, B_int=r*q+a, B_joint=r*(2k-r-1)/(2*(t+1)), and d_N=1+W+max(A0,min(B_int,floor(B_joint))). The complete disperser proof needs prime k>r+1, verified in disperser.md Section15; the evaluator explicitly enforces this weaker guard. All guards and k>=t(t+1)/2 hold eventually, k=Theta(N^(3/5)), and eventually d_N=1+W+A0=(t-1)k+(r*(r+1)-t*(t-1))/2+1. Consequently liminf over ALL integer N of C_B2(F_N)/N>=4. More precisely put b=c^(1/5) and M=sqrt(b)+1/(2*b^2). For every epsilon>0, C_B2(F_N)>=4N-(8M+epsilon)*N^(4/5) at every sufficiently large integer N; the proved remainder R_N=3k+8d_N-7 has limsup R_N/N^(4/5)<=8M<8*sqrt(2)+1. This is a certified uniform remainder envelope for this single new family, not a pointwise complexity comparison with another language. The generic additive-seven theorem for d>=3 uses exactly the four normalized R84 refutations and complete Q7 coverage executed by audit.py, with complete normalization and unrestricted-sharing transfer in elimination.md. Every prefix bit is eventually essential and fixing an accepted prefix with nonconstant residual removes at least k gates in the strengthened signed-wire/output-literal model. All field, prefix, dispersion, guard and all-length arguments are supplied. No prime number theorem or conjectural gap hypothesis is used.","version":"circuitbreaker-expression-v1"}

experiments.purpose: Regenerate/refute all four normalized R84 CNFs and cover every one of4082400 normalized Q7 read-once assignments by checked legal flats. These predicates support only the two finite lemmas; universal normalization and gate transfer are supplied in elimination.md.
